description: Phase 5 evidence: the Pixel Asset authoring contract, its validation, the attachment model, three reference assets and the dev review mode.

builtInCharacterWrapped.approach: The existing sprite tables are wrapped by a spans geometry, not rewritten as rasters.
builtInCharacterWrapped.why: The body is a shaded silhouette whose highlight boundary is derived from each row width, and the eyes are six shapes selected by state. Rasterising would lose the derived shading or freeze it at one size.
tests: every authored Sylf state has an asset state
the face is separate planes, not whole-character frames
every state still composes the body
the widest body row is still 30 columns
the asset resolves using content-layer helpers only

validation.failsClosed: An unknown palette token is an error even though the resolver skips it, because a mistyped key that silently paints nothing is the failure mode being prevented.
validation.limits: Integer coordinates, bounds, dimensions, palette references, unique ids, plane references, anchors, size limits and state/variant references. Semantic intent (is the grip where a hand goes?) is the review panel job, not the validator.

attachment.model: offset = host.anchor - attachment.pivot, in reference space
attachment.thenPaintedWith: the host placement (its origin AND scale), so an attachment is sized by what holds it
attachment.defectFound: The first implementation gave a placed asset the host scale but not its origin. Because the offset is a reference-space delta, an origin of zero silently turned it into a display coordinate and the wand rendered across the character face at the wrong size.
attachment.defectFix: A placed asset inherits a whole placement, not a scale.

capabilities: anchor marks from the painter own mapping
held item attached to a character
density 32/40/48/64 at a fixed presentation size
reviewTooling.drawsThrough: paintAsset, the same entry point a production consumer uses

unchanged: engine, renderer, runtime and React host
no persistence, Pixel Studio, Character Customizer, cosmetics migration or Sylf redesign
limitations: Ambient scenery is character planes rather than its own asset. Fine for one presentation; if scenery becomes shared it wants to be a separate asset painted first.
A reference grid is authored per asset, so a pivot meaning is relative to its own asset grid. Attachment is what bridges them.
Validation cannot check semantic intent; the review panel is the answer to that class of mistake.

openDecisions.unchanged: O1-O18 were not informed by this phase.
openDecisions.O19: New: whether scenery becomes its own asset kind. Deferred until an asset demonstrates the need.
openDecisions.O20: New: whether an asset may compose another asset. Today an asset is flat and attachment is positional only; composition would be a real contract extension and is deferred.
alsoDeferred: a catalogue index beyond a hand-written list
per-asset revision history, which is persistence and out of scope
